read.skipped: nothing; the chapter PDF has no reference list, so citations are bracket keys only

question: How is RL used to improve LLMs (RLFT, reward models, thinking models, single- and multi-turn algorithms), and how are LLMs used inside RL agents?
contributions: Survey of RL fine-tuning of LLMs: reward types, PPO/GRPO/DAPO/GSPO/RLOO/REINFORCE++/VinePPO/DPO, inference-time scaling as posterior sampling, multi-turn RL
Survey of LLMs for RL (input processing, rewards, world models, policies) and efficient sequence models
Worked Tinker/GEM policy-gradient implementation with a guess-the-number example

limits: No reference list in the PDF: all citations are bracket keys.
Author says the field is fast growing and only highlights are covered (p147).
VinePPO is slow and not general purpose (p153).
DPO is limited to preference data (p155).
Only multi-turn LLM RL papers listed are few; the area is expected to grow (p157).
Tinker example is one run on an easy game, no seeds or error bars; o1/o3 details are not public (p149-150).
practices: Prefer RLFT over SFT where verification is easier than generation, for thinking actions, and for generalisation (p147).
Use binary verifiable rewards for math (answer equality) and code (unit tests) (p148).
Keep the policy near the reference with a per-token KL penalty -beta*KL (p151, p154).
Do not add the KL penalty to the advantage; modify the token-level reward instead (p169).
Use the k2 KL estimator when gradients matter since k3 has a biased gradient (p154).
Drop std division (Dr GRPO) or use a leave-one-out baseline to avoid difficulty bias (p153).
Use asymmetric clip with eps_high 0.28 to keep exploration (p152).
Use sequence-level importance ratio (GSPO) when reward is trajectory-level (p152).
For long-horizon multi-turn tasks truncate or summarise history and learn a critic with GAE, warm-starting actor from an instruct model (p158).
Average loss over transitions, not tokens, to avoid bias to long thinking traces (p167).
Monitor KL(q||p) and policy entropy during training (p169).
Handle invalid actions by truncating, restarting from the failure state, or resampling the action (p158).

terms.definition: reinforcement learning fine-tuning: training the LLM with RL using a suitable reward function
RL with verifiable rewards, binary reward from answer equality or unit tests
process reward model: reward on partial trajectories (dense); outcome reward model: reward on final sequence (sparse)
learning a reward model from human preference data (Bradley-Terry), then using RL to maximise it
RL from AI feedback, with an LLM as judge giving preferences or rewards
generative reward model: predicts reward and returns its chain of thought
Group Relative PPO: replaces the critic with group-mean/std normalised MC advantage
Group Sequence Policy Optimization: sequence-level length-normalised importance ratio
Reinforce Leave-One-Out: baseline is the mean reward of the other samples
MC value estimates from rollouts reset at any intermediate state
Direct Preference Optimization: fits the policy to preferences with loss -log sigma(beta log ratio_w - beta log ratio_l)
particle filtering with a twist function predicting future reward, for sampling the tilted posterior
return batch normalization, a multi-turn variant of GRPO
LLM-generated code that represents the world model
time to first token: prefill latency, O(N^2)
